pains.statement: Order-to-cash or inventory go-live caused shipment freezes and manual order re-entry under executive deadline pressure.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Name go-live date, slips, and first production process that failed (shipment, invoice, allocation).

pains.statement: Dozens of WMS, EDI, and CRM adapters were discovered late—integrations entered UAT without parallel-run time.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Count production adapters; name one that failed in week one post go-live.

pains.statement: Product or pricing fields migrated with different commercial meaning in the new ERP, causing silent allocation errors.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Give one field pair and the downstream report or fulfillment error.

pains.statement: Regional ops manually reconciles ERP inventory against warehouse truth because batch interfaces disagree.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Hours per week spent re-keying; which SKU family or region.

pains.statement: Leadership funded a global ERP program but cannot name a bounded stabilization deliverable after go-live failure.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Quote the transformation mandate vs what is actually funded this quarter.

pains.statement: Excessive ERP customization makes every upgrade and patch a multi-month regression event.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Count custom objects or change orders; last upgrade duration.

pains.statement: A second big-bang cutover is politically impossible after the first production failure.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Past rollback story or executive 'no outage window' memo.

pains.statement: Finance close and ops reporting lag because extracts from the new ERP disagree with legacy subledgers.
pains.suggestedEvidence: Close cycle extension; which report pair disagrees.
